architecture_decisions: Separate safe patch preparation from multi-file orchestration; validate before mutation, recheck preimages, rollback failures, and emit deterministic evidence.
work_items: Create a bounded text-patch engine that safely mutates an isolated workspace and emits deterministic implementation evidence without gaining protected stage or release authority.
validations: Ensure the engine rejects path escape, stale input, malformed patches, unsupported targets, excessive sizes, and partial multi-file success.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — Targets stay inside the declared workspace. Every accepted target is a relative workspace path whose lexical and resolved location remains under the workspace root; absolute paths, traversal, NULs, Git internals, and symlink-based escape are rejected before mutation.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — Each patch binds to an exact pre-image digest. Existing-file preparation requires the caller's expected base SHA-256 to equal the current file digest; new-file creation requires the SHA-256 of empty content, and any mismatch fails before mutation.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — Only bounded UTF-8 source targets are eligible. Binary content, unsupported target types/extensions, directories, secret-sensitive targets, and source or result sizes beyond configured limits fail closed.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — Only a strict single-target unified diff is accepted. Headers must match the declared target and hunks must be ordered, non-overlapping, count-consistent, exact against the base, and produce a real change; malformed, multi-file, conflicting, or no-op patches fail without mutation.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Existing text files may be modified and bounded new text files may be created. New files must be beneath an already-existing safe parent, use `/dev/null` as the old side, and cannot overwrite an existing target through creation semantics.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — Successful application returns deterministic observable evidence. Evidence includes target and created state, before/after SHA-256 and byte sizes, patch SHA-256 and size, bounded unified diff, aggregate source/patch/result sizes, and artifact path/digest/size; equivalent inputs produce equivalent evidence.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — Multi-file requests are all-or-nothing. Duplicate targets are rejected, every patch is prepared before any mutation, each target is atomically replaced, and already-written targets are restored if a later commit fails; partial application is never reported as protected success.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Per-file and aggregate resource use is explicitly bounded. Maximum patch, source-file, result-file, request-file-count, aggregate-source, aggregate-patch, and aggregate-result limits are checked before mutation so input cannot cause unbounded mutation or evidence growth.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — The engine adds no execution or release authority. It exposes no user/model-supplied shell, arbitrary HTTP/network, Git history mutation or push/merge, provider credential handling, Work Specification self-approval, Vercel promotion, or production deployment operation.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Engine evidence is integration-ready but does not authorize IMPLEMENT. The result exposes a deterministic artifact list and workspace digest for later protected mapping while remaining independent of Project persistence and autonomy/service/state-machine internals until #43 and other Wave 1 contracts stabilize.
risks: This implementation does not connect to the autonomy coordinator or grant Git, shell, network, deployment, Work Specification approval, or production authority.
